pages.title: Read Me
pages.subtitle: Set up once, then protect the block

blocks.heading: Choose your size
paragraphs: Four sizes are included and all four contain identical pages. A4 and US Letter suit the desk. A5 and Half Letter suit a tablet or a bag, and print two-up on a full sheet.

blocks.heading: Digital use
items: Open the PDF in GoodNotes, Notability, Noteshelf, Xodo or any app that imports PDFs
Import as a document, not as an image
Switch the app to read mode to tap links, and write mode to write
Use the Session tab to reach a blank session plan from anywhere
Tap Contents in the footer to return to the index

blocks.heading: Printing
items: Print at 100% scale and never select fit to page
Use 100 to 120 gsm paper for double-sided printing
Print the daily set once and reprint it as needed — the pages are undated

pages.title: How To Use
pages.subtitle: The focus cycle, four steps

blocks.heading: Before the day — ten minutes
items: Read the current Priority Planner page
Write Today's Focus — one sentence, not a list
Set the three Most Important Tasks
Block the day, hardest work into your best hours

blocks.heading: Before each block — two minutes
items: Fill a Focus Session Planner: the goal, the finish line, the length
Clear the environment named on your Recovery Plan
Start the clock and close this planner

blocks.heading: After each block — three minutes
items: Log the session in the Deep Focus Log while it is fresh
Record anything that pulled you away in the Distraction Tracker
Take the break you planned, before the next block, not instead of it

blocks.heading: End of week — twenty minutes
paragraphs: Fill the Weekly Focus Review, then the Progress Dashboard. The dashboard is where the pattern appears: which hours actually held attention, and which interruptions are structural rather than accidental.

pages.title: Focus Principles
pages.subtitle: Six rules this planner is built on

blocks.heading: One thing, finished
paragraphs: Attention does not divide, it alternates — and every switch costs minutes you never see leave. This planner gives one focus per day and three tasks, because a list of ten is a list of none.

blocks.heading: Protect the hours, not the intention
paragraphs: Motivation is not a plan. A block on a page with a start time, an end time and a stated finish line is a plan.

blocks.heading: Distraction is data
paragraphs: Log what pulled you away and whether it came from inside or outside. Internal distraction is answered by rest. External distraction is answered by a boundary.

blocks.heading: Breaks are part of the work
items: A break taken on purpose ends when you decide
A break taken by collapse ends when the day does
Screen breaks are not breaks
The break is planned before the block starts

blocks.heading: Energy sets the ceiling
paragraphs: No system out-plans exhaustion. Track energy for two weeks and put the hardest work where the energy already is, rather than where the calendar happens to be empty.

blocks.heading: Review or repeat
paragraphs: Without the weekly review, a bad pattern simply runs again next week with a new set of pages.
